cues.text: A small village, a big choice
Andrés Iniesta grew up in Fuentealbilla, a small village in Spain.
There were no proper football pitches there, so he mostly played futsal, a small-sided game on a hard court.
At twelve, playing for Albacete in a seven-a-side tournament, he was noticed by scouts.
His parents knew a Barcelona youth coach, Enrique Orizaola.
Open the farmhouse door.
Together, the family visited La Masia, the farmhouse where Barcelona’s young players live, and they decided he would go.
Big choices feel easier when you make them together with the people who love you.
Crying rivers
When the day came to leave for La Masia, Andrés later said, he cried rivers.
At the academy he found it very hard to be apart from his parents.
He was very shy, and he kept to himself.
Clear the rain cloud.
Missing home does not mean you are weak.
It shows how much you love the people you left behind.
Andrés stayed at the academy, and he kept training with the other boys.
It’s okay to cry. Tears are a sign that you care, not a sign that you are weak.
Quiet, and a captain
Being shy did not stop Andrés.
In 1999 he was captain of Barcelona’s under-15 team at the Nike Premier Cup.
In the final, he scored the winning goal in the last minute, and he was named the best player of the tournament.
Pass the captain’s armband.
Soon after Andrés arrived, the first-team captain, Pep Guardiola, told his teammate Xavi that this boy would one day take all their places.
Quiet people can be brave leaders too.
Being quiet is not a weakness. You can lead in your own way.
Losing a friend
By 2009, Andrés was a star for Barcelona and Spain, but he had been injured again and again.
Then, on 8 August 2009, his close friend Dani Jarque, a fellow footballer and the captain of Espanyol, died.
Light a star for Dani.
For a long time afterwards, Andrés felt very low.
Even when his body was fit, some days he could not finish training.
Sadness like this can make even the strongest people feel tired and empty.
When you feel sad for a long time, it’s not your fault, and you don’t have to hide it.
Asking for help
Andrés did not try to get better alone.
He asked for help, including from a psychologist, Inma Puig.
A psychologist’s job is to help people with their thoughts and feelings.
Knock on the helper’s door.
Years later, in 2018, Andrés spoke openly about it in an interview.
He said he had suffered from depression before the 2010 World Cup, because of his injuries and the death of his friend.
Speaking up helps other people know they are not alone.
Asking for help is brave. Talking to someone you trust can make heavy feelings lighter.
Always with us
In 2010, Spain played the Netherlands in the World Cup final, and Andrés scored the winning goal.
He pulled up his shirt to show a message written on the shirt underneath: Dani Jarque, always with us.
Lift the shirt to see the message.
He said it showed that being a good person matters more than rivalry, or your team, or your colours.
Later, even the fans at Espanyol, Barcelona’s local rivals, stood and clapped for him because of his friendship with Dani.
The people we love stay with us. Kindness is bigger than any rivalry.
